newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran inflation up at annual rate of 18.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Iran inflation up at annual rate of 18.8 percent.

text.p: Consumer inflation in Iranian cities rose to an annual rate of 18.8 percent in the month to June 21, versus an annual 17.7 percent the previous month, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Sunday.
Quoting a Central Bank of Iran statistics report, IRNA said prices rose by a month-on-month 0.5 percent in the period May 22 to June 21, 1997.
"The report added that inflation rate in the first quarter of the current year reached 17.1 percent, showing a slight increase compared to the preceding year," IRNA said.

Steep price rises are a common complaint and the government has come under attack in the press and parliament for not doing enough to fight inflation, which Iranian officials have said is a top priority.
Inflation in the last Iranian year to March 1997 stood at 23.2 percent against 49.4 percent the year before, the central bank governor has said.
